### D15. Cote 54, scan 8, reused sheet, Corollaries 2–3

**Kind:** own idea. **Quote:** “Il suffit d'appliquer la prop. 10”. **Status:** elementary editorial comparison; provenance unassigned.

For a locally finite arrangement of affine hyperplanes in a finite-dimensional real space, compactness of a segment reduces its crossings to finitely many hyperplanes.
At a point in the relative interior of a wall and on no other hyperplane, a sufficiently small ball has exactly two local sides; connectedness of that relative interior then explains constancy of the adjacent chamber in Corollary 3.
**Confidence: high** under these explicit topological hypotheses; this argument does not identify the sheet's author, publication, or a reflection-group structure.

Nondegeneracy of $\varphi$ and $Q$ alone does not give the displayed algebra: take $V=\mathbb Q e\oplus\mathbb Q f$, $W=0$, and $\varphi(e,f)=1$.

heading: D17. Cote 16, scan 27, isotropic-line special case
text:
### D17. Cote 16, scan 27, isotropic-line special case

**Kind:** own idea. **Quote:** “une droite isotrope $D$”. **Status:** explicit editorial realization of the stated algebraic case.

Over $\mathbb Q$, take $\widetilde W=\mathbb Q\xi\oplus\mathbb Q w$ with $\widetilde Q=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, any symplectic form $\varphi$ on an even-dimensional $V$, and $\alpha(x\wedge y)=\varphi(x,y)(\xi+w)$.
Then $\alpha^*\widetilde Q=0$, but $\widetilde Q(\xi,\xi)=1$ and $\widetilde Q(\alpha(x\wedge y),\xi)=\varphi(x,y)$, so the two nondegeneracy requirements hold while $\chi=0$.
**Confidence: high**, by these identities; the example distinguishes nondegeneracy of the ambient form from that of $\chi'$ and asserts no geometric realization.

heading: D18. Cote 16, scan 29, tensor square and orbit assertion
text:
### D18. Cote 16, scan 29, tensor square and orbit assertion

**Kind:** reading question. **Quote:** “dim non bornée”. **Status:** editorial distinction and normalization warning.

For fixed finite $V$, Cayley–Hamilton bounds every cyclic span in $\bigwedge^2V$ by $\binom{\dim V}{2}$, although the orbit as a set can be infinite over an infinite field; over a finite field every such orbit is finite.
The manuscript's unboundedness must therefore be assessed as $\dim V$ grows, as its parenthesis indicates.
The tensor square in $\bigwedge^*V\otimes\bigwedge^*V$ also requires a stated multiplication and antisymmetrization convention: multiplying an operator by a nonzero scalar preserves its cyclic spans but can change finite-orbit behavior.
**Editorial confidence: high**, from finite-dimensional linear algebra; the following tests use an explicit normalized operator, not an imposed reading of $u$.

heading: D19. Cote 16, scan 29, “$4$ (ou $6$?)”: a conditional six-dimensional test
text:
### D19. Cote 16, scan 29, “$4$ (ou $6$?)”: a conditional six-dimensional test

**Kind:** own idea. **Quote:** “$\chi'$ non dégénérée”. **Status:** verified algebraic example conditional on the operator convention.

Let $V=\bigoplus_{i=1}^3(\mathbb Qe_i\oplus\mathbb Qf_i)$, $p_i=e_i\wedge f_i$, $\mathbf1=\sum p_i$, and define
\[
C=\frac23\begin{pmatrix}0&1&2\\1&0&3\\2&3&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
\chi=\sum_{i<j}C_{ij}e_i^*\wedge f_i^*\wedge e_j^*\wedge f_j^*,\quad
Q(a,b)=\chi(a\wedge b),\quad \xi=\tfrac12(p_2+p_3).
\]
Then $Q(\xi,\xi)=1$, $\varphi(x,y)=Q(x\wedge y,\xi)=\sum_i(e_i^*\wedge f_i^*)(x,y)$, and $Q$ is nondegenerate, with determinant $2097152/59049$ in the induced exterior basis.
Set $\varphi^\sharp=(v\mapsto\varphi(\,·\,,v))^{-1}$, $Q^\flat(a)=Q(\,·\,,a)$, and $U=(\bigwedge^2\varphi^\sharp)Q^\flat$; under contraction $\iota_{e_i^*}(e_i\wedge f_i)=f_i$, the inverse bivector is $\mathbf1$, and on $\langle p_1,p_2,p_3\rangle$ one computes
\[
U=C,\quad U\xi=\mathbf1,\quad
\det[\mathbf1,C\mathbf1,C^2\mathbf1]=-32/27,\quad
C\mathbf1=(2,8/3,10/3)^t.
\]
Thus both orbits are infinite, since $C^r\mathbf1\ge2^r\mathbf1$ coordinatewise, and their cyclic spans have dimension three; **editorial confidence: high** for this specified $U$, from exact rational identities, without a claim of Hodge positivity or geometric realization.

heading: D20. Cote 16, scan 29, final growing-dimension parenthesis
text:
### D20. Cote 16, scan 29, final growing-dimension parenthesis

**Kind:** own idea. **Quote:** “quand” [uncertain reading] “$\dim V$”. **Status:** conditional unbounded-family construction.

For any $m\ge2$, start with the $2m\times2m$ block matrix $C_0=\operatorname{diag}(d_j\begin{psmallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{psmallmatrix})_{j=1}^m$, with distinct rational $1\le d_j\le2$; the all-ones vector has cyclic span $m$, by a Vandermonde minor.
Replace every off-block zero by a sufficiently small positive rational $\varepsilon$, obtaining $C_\varepsilon$, and put $s=\mathbf1^tC_\varepsilon^{-1}\mathbf1$, $C=sC_\varepsilon$, $\xi=C^{-1}\mathbf1$; invertibility, positivity of $s$, and that nonzero minor persist.
On $V=\bigoplus_{i=1}^{2m}(\mathbb Qe_i\oplus\mathbb Qf_i)$ use $p_i=e_i\wedge f_i$ for coordinates, define $\chi=\sum_{i<j}C_{ij}e_i^*\wedge f_i^*\wedge e_j^*\wedge f_j^*$ and $Q(a,b)=\chi(a\wedge b)$, and obtain
\[
\det Q=\det C\prod_{i<j}C_{ij}^{4}\ne0,\qquad
Q(\xi,\xi)=1,\qquad
\varphi(x,y):=Q(x\wedge y,\xi)=\sum_i(e_i^*\wedge f_i^*)(x,y),\qquad
U|_{\langle p_i\rangle}=C,\qquad U\xi=\mathbf1,
\]
where $Q^\flat(a)=Q(\,·\,,a)$, $\varphi^\sharp=(v\mapsto\varphi(\,·\,,v))^{-1}$, and $U=(\bigwedge^2\varphi^\sharp)Q^\flat$.
The cyclic spans therefore have dimension at least $m$ as $\dim V=4m$ grows, and the positive normalized row sums exceed one for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, giving infinite set-orbits too; **editorial confidence: high** for this normalized construction, by the nonzero minor and block determinants, without settling additional Hodge or geometric constraints.

heading: Q07 — A precisely specified quadratic×quadratic product is impossible
text:
### Q07 — A precisely specified quadratic×quadratic product is impossible

**Cote 45, scan 068, final “?!?” · Kind: own idea; confidence high, by polar expansion and independent exhaustive calculation.**

Let H=F₂e⊕F₂f with q(xe+yf)=xy and let s exchange e and f; no quadratic Q on H⊗H can satisfy both Q(v⊗w)=q(v)q(w) for every v,w and invariance under s⊗id. Indeed the pure-tensor rule gives B_Q((e+f)⊗e,(e+f)⊗f)=1, while expanding the polar form leaves two cross terms exchanged by s⊗id and hence equal, whose sum in F₂ is zero. Enumeration of all 1,024 quadratic polynomials on F₂⁴ finds exactly two satisfying the pure-tensor rule, z₀z₃ and z₁z₂ in the ordered basis (e⊗e,e⊗f,f⊗e,f⊗f), which that involution exchanges; this tests the stated naturality specification, not every construction with extra data. CT **16:027/029** supplies bilinear/exterior operations but no such tensor rule, and [EKM, p. 51] instead supplies the bilinear×quadratic operation, so this is a substantive response to the current question with a sharply limited conclusion.

### R05 — A one-dimensional hermitian test detects an internal sign inconsistency

**Cote 45, scans 058/060, formulas (8) and (12) · Kind: own idea / reading question; confidence high for the test.**

heading: N16 — Finite presentation makes local freeness automatic
text:
### N16 — Finite presentation makes local freeness automatic

**Kind:** own verification answering a manuscript question. **File/scan:** 46:009, final paragraph; compare 008's isomorphism $E^{(p)}\to E$. **State:** no directly matching settled entry; WG2 §1.1 #3; methodological link to context 16:052.

For a finitely presented module M over any characteristic-p ring R, an isomorphism $F_R^*M\simeq M$ implies finite local freeness: base change of Fitting ideals gives $I_i=I_i^{[p]}$, where $I_i=\operatorname{Fitt}_i(M)$ and $I^{[p]}$ is generated by p-th powers. Each I_i is finitely generated, and at a local ring a proper I_i satisfies $I_i^{[p]}\subseteq\mathfrak m I_i$, so Nakayama makes it zero; the Fitting criterion then gives freeness locally. This answers part of “les hypothèses de locale liberté et de type fini” and connects concretely to the Fitting/base-change discussion in context 16:052 (§2 nos. 1–2; notes 16:52:1, 16:52:4, R14), without attributing the proof to that sheet. **Confidence: high**, by this explicit argument and an independent proof check; The Stacks Project Authors (2026a, Lemmas 15.8.4,15.8.8; 2026b, Lemma 51.17.1) supply the Fitting facts and the Noetherian local finite-module version, respectively.

heading: N17 — Finite generation alone admits a counterexample
text:
### N17 — Finite generation alone admits a counterexample

**Kind:** own verification. **File/scan:** 46:009, same question. **State:** no directly matching settled entry; same methodological context as N16.

Let $R=\mathbf F_p[t^{1/p^n}:n\geq0]$, $I=(t^{1/p^n}:n\geq0)$, and $M=R/I\cong\mathbf F_p$; then $I=I^{[p]}$ gives $F_R^*M\cong M$, although M is cyclic and not locally free at I. Indeed, R is a domain and the nonzero element t kills the nonzero module $M_I$, while $I=\bigcup_n(t^{1/p^n})$ is a strictly increasing union, explaining why M is not finitely presented. This sharpens the question in Hua's Frobenius-vector-bundle subsection and complements the finite-presentation result rather than conflicting with it. **Confidence: high**, because all assertions follow directly from the displayed ring and ideal; a detailed proof is retained in `records/research/frobenius_module_check.md`.

**Kind:** own verification / reading question. **File/scan:** 46:011, final ideal calculation. **State:** no direct entry; context 16:052 supplies an adjacent finite-generation method.

### N31 — The normal-case injectivity question is answered on the continuation

**Kind:** self-flagged, subsequently addressed. **File/scan:** 46:020, “Cet hom est-il injectif?”; 021, opening. **State:** no direct settled entry; WG2 §1.1 #3.

Normality makes a rational p-th root of a regular function regular by integrality, and for a unit the inverse root is regular as well, completing the opening continuation's dlog injectivity argument. ### N32 — The final quotient on scan 021 is noninjective as literally written

**Kind:** own verification. **File/scan:** 46:021, final display. **State:** no direct entry; WG2 §1.1 #3.

The asserted injection starts from “$\mathcal R_X^*/\underline O_X^*$”, but rational p-th powers already map to zero under the logarithmic derivative. In the regular local ring $\mathbf F_p[t]_{(t)}$, the nonunit rational function $t^p$ gives a nonzero class modulo units and zero logarithmic differential, so that displayed map is not injective. The proposed factorization $f=g^ph$ instead points to the quotient by $\mathcal O_X^*\mathcal R_X^{*p}$, as Hua's Picard discussion also recognizes. **Confidence: high**, by this explicit regular-ring example; it identifies an omitted quotient factor, not a counterexample to the corrected local problem.

### N41 — Picard p-torsion points do not recover the full group scheme

**Kind:** unpursued implication. **File/scan:** 46:020–022; context 54:005,007. **State:** WG2 §1.1 #3.

“Détermination de ${}_p\operatorname{Pic}(X)$” concerns p-torsion line-bundle classes, whereas Oda's Corollary 5.12 concerns the group-scheme kernel $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}[p]$ and its dual Dieudonné module $D M(\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}[p])$. For smooth proper X over a perfect field k of characteristic p with a k-point, that module maps into de Rham cohomology with image the classes whose successive Cartier iterates remain closed, written $\bigcap_{n\ge1}\ker(d\circ V^n)$ in Oda's iteratively defined sense; V is not an endomorphism of all $H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}$ in this generality (Oda, 1969, Definition 3.5, p. 82; Definitions 5.6–5.8, pp. 122–124; Corollary 5.12, p. 131). This adds an essential infinitesimal distinction to Hua's Picard discussion and the earlier A[p] context.

heading: N52 — The degree-one criterion is a close published parallel

### N52 — The degree-one criterion is a close published parallel

**Kind:** unpursued implication / literature comparison. **File/scan:** 46:041, proposition 2. **State:** WG2 §1.1 #3.

The criterion “de degré 1 sur chaque fibre” and its formula with the top exterior power of differentials isolate the obstruction to a projective form being a projective bundle. heading: N53 — The section argument passes through the dual incidence divisor

### N53 — The section argument passes through the dual incidence divisor

**Kind:** unproved claim with published comparison. **File/scan:** 46:041, proposition 3. **State:** WG2 §1.1 #3; LM6 F.6 only as a boundary.

## XII. Method and verification record

The primary agent visually read every supplied whole image and both supplied halves in scan order, produced each page and its inventory before proceeding, and then performed the required second reading of all 42 faces. No manuscript OCR was used, and no transcription or image audit was delegated. Research support was delegated only after the freeze; the support records identify their scope and do not edit the frozen page files.

The combined TeX remains a fragment without a preamble. A structural check found no unbalanced braces, mismatched environments, or the other tested syntax issues, and all 136 diagram arrows were included in the technical review. **A TeX compile/render was not completed:** the available XeLaTeX executable failed before reading the manuscript because the format file and required TeX installation were absent; the harness and failure output are retained under records/technical, so this package makes no claim of successful rendering.

The doubts file identifies the weakest regions, especially the plan on 003, cancelled headings on 029 and 038, the margin on 045, and several passages on 047. TikZ drawings reproduce shapes and placement approximately; they do not claim facsimile identity. The 625 inventory rows all read “yes”, indicating inclusion rather than a guarantee that every difficult reading is correct.

The immutable transcription manifest is records/transcription.sha256. The final progress-log entry records verification of all 42 page hashes and the combined-fragment hash against the freeze; any later reading change belongs to a future explicitly revised transcription, not to these research notes.
